subject: Embed/rerank handoff: index reconciliation, DB choices, and fallback experiments
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@heliopay.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embed/rerank handoff: index reconciliation, DB choices, and fallback experiments

Asha — thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our Handoff checklist I wanted to capture an initial plan so CS, Eng (runtime + infra), and HelioPay infra are aligned before our implementation sprint. High-level asks below; please flag any mismatches.

Summary / goals:
- Get embeddings index to parity in Prod (backfill ~18M docs) with minimal query impact (target: <150ms p95).
- Layer reranker (lightweight re-rank) behind feature flag; A/B compare quality uplift on a 5% traffic slice.
- Maintain customer SLA during backfill; automated fallback to cached vector-store queries when node pressure > 60%.

Key decision points we need to confirm this week:
1) Vector DB choice for primary index: HelioPay prefers managed cluster (they mentioned Weaviate). We need to validate hot reload performance and snapshot/restore cadence; if we go multi-DB (primary + fallback), define TTL & sync window.
2) Backfill window & throttling: recommended approach is phased waves by customer segment (A/B/C), with per-shard concurrency limits. Expect ~72 hours for first wave of 4M docs on our Dedicated pool (estimate).
3) Rerank eval plan & sample set: attached rerank-sample-suite-v2.jsonl — please review sampling bias across payment dispute docs. We propose 2 evaluation rounds (staging smoke + 1-week production A/B).

Initial action owners:
- HelioPay (Asha/infra): confirm DB topology, whitelist Redwood Dedicated IPs, provide sample export (1M docs) by Tue EOD.
- Jordan (runtime): prepare warmstart script for KV cache priming and safe throttles.
- Karthik (onboard ops): finalize priming windows and rollback playbook.
- Ben (CS): coordinate internal stakeholders and QA acceptance criteria.

Attachments: helio-priming-window-spec.csv, rerank-sample-suite-v2.jsonl, vector-db-compat-matrix.pdf

Thanks — I’ll schedule a short sync for Wed to lock the timelines.

— Evelyn Hart
Senior Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha@heliopay.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embed/rerank handoff: index reconciliation, DB choices, and fallback experiments

Thanks Evelyn — quick technical notes from the runtime side after a first pass on the sample export and the vector-db-compat-matrix.pdf. I ran a micro-bench on a 100k slice and captured the following observations: 

- Weaviate (managed) works but cold-query p95 is higher than our Dedicated LM path because of network hops; caching will be crucial.
- If HelioPay uses an external DB, we should deploy a thin local vector cache with prefix/nearest-neighbor cache for the 20% most-frequent queries (we can seed from their query logs). This reduces p95 by ~40% in our tests.
- Backfill approach: use a staggered wave pattern by user segment and index shard. Each worker process will do: embed -> write to DB -> validate checksum -> update index manifest. We recommend a per-worker batch size of 2k docs for memory+GPU constraints; concurrency cap of 12 workers per host.
- Estimated durations (rough): 4M docs -> ~18 hours (Dedicated pool), 18M docs -> ~3.5 days with a 10% buffer. Network egress and DB write QPS are the main throttles.

Rollback & fallback:
- If write latency causes >3% error rate on live queries, switch to read-through fallback that queries the previous index snapshot and returns cached rerank results. We will expose a feature-flag toggle in Console for quick cutover.

Next steps for us:
- I’ll push the warmstart KV priming script to the repo and attach a runbook.
- Need HelioPay to confirm acceptability of a local cache instance (small VM) or allow our Dedicated service to act as the primary vector store during backfill waves.

Jordan
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Asha Rao <asha@heliopay.com>

Subject: Re: Embed/rerank handoff: index reconciliation, DB choices, and fallback experiments

Appreciate the clarity — we reviewed the compatibility matrix and ran a quick internal check. A few confirmations and asks from our side: 

1) We prefer to keep the primary index in our managed Weaviate cluster for compliance. We can provision a temporary higher-throughput tier for the backfill but need a clear rollback plan.
2) Local cache sounds acceptable if it stays behind our VPC and does not persist PII beyond the agreed TTL. Can you confirm TTL defaults and encryption at rest for the cache VM?
3) Rerank sample: the attached JSONL looks good but we need stratified sampling to ensure edge cases (chargebacks, disputed refunds) are over-sampled by 2x.

Logistics: our infra team can provide the sample export by Mon 05/31 EOD. We can also open a temporary peering connection for the Dedicated pool — will coordinate with infra@heliopay.com.

Action items from HelioPay:
- infra@heliopay.com: provide sample export + allow Redwood IPs for peering test.
- Product (Asha): share prioritized user segments for wave ordering by EOD Mon.

We are ok to run a small staging smoke (50k docs) as soon as Jordan pushes the warmstart script.

— Asha
Head of PM, HelioPay

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha@heliopay.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-31T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embed/rerank handoff: index reconciliation, DB choices, and fallback experiments

Quick operational plan to lock timelines and acceptance criteria (per requests above). Please review and sign off: 

Planned schedule:
- Mon 05/31: HelioPay provides sample export + segment priority. Redwood runs 50k staging smoke (validate mapping + rerank sample).
- Tue 06/01 09:00 - 12:00: Run wave 1 (4M docs) on Dedicated with local cache priming; monitor write QPS and p95.
- Wed 06/02 - Thu 06/03: Continue waves 2 & 3 (staggered), run rerank A/B on 5% traffic after wave 1 stabilizes for 24h.

Acceptance criteria (for go/no-go between waves):
- Query p95 <= 150ms for baseline routes OR fallback triggers with <1% user-visible errors.
- Rerank A/B: at least one metric (NDCG@10 or click-lift proxy) shows >=5% improvement in staging before full rollout.
- No more than 0.5% of customer requests impacted during backfill (measured by error rate / retries).

Rollback process:
- Immediate: flip feature flag to route to pre-backfill snapshot and disable rerank layer for impacted endpoints.
- If persistent issues: pause backfill waves and run a targeted rebuild on affected shards with lower concurrency.

Please reply with explicit sign-off on the schedule and acceptance criteria. If we get HelioPay sign-off by EOD today, we’ll proceed with the 50k smoke Tue morning and report results by Tue afternoon.

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Onboard Ops
Redwood Inference
